newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen stable, BOJ seen accommodative.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen stable, BOJ seen accommodative.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen futures were stable in late Monday trade while the Japanese government bond futures (JGBs) ended firmer.
Euroyen and JGBs futures were locked in a narrow two-tick range given the lack of fresh trading factors, dealers said.
Earlier comments by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita at the opening of the two-day meeting with BOJ branch managers had little impact on the markets, they added.
"What Matsushita said was not new. He just reconfirmed Japan's accommodative monetary policy," a Japanese dealer said.
At 1115 GMT, the December Euroyen was around 99.07 against its previous IMM close at 99.06. Turnover was around 5,000 lots.
Dealers said a European trader was actively buying 11,000 lots of June Euroyen put options with a 99.25 strike price, which capped Euroyen's upside. They would expire on June 16.
SIMEX floor traders said the purchase appeared to be more of a position squaring than a fresh position taken on expectations of a flat near term yield curve.
"We noticed the party had sold the options before and now they are buying back," said a dealer.
Dealers expected December Euroyen to trade sideways but with more downside potential. It was expected to test 99.01/99.02.
"If this level is sustained, December would firm back towards 99.14," he said.
A robust Japanese stock market and BOJ's restrain from its daily monetary operations which left a 190 billion yen surplus in the banking reserves, also capped Euroyen futures, dealers said.
June JGBs ended at 126.90 against its previous close at 126.84 on a paltry turnover of 91 lots.

Dealers said activity was subdued as the market awaited the possible bond issue by Tokyo Electric Power Co Ltd (TEPCO) later this week. TEPCO was expected to launch about 150-200 billion yen worth of bonds.
December Eurodollars ended in line with its previous IMM close, at 93.520.
